issues.legal_issue: The court-fee payable in a partition suit must be determined from the plaint read as a whole, rather than from the written statement or the eventual decision on the merits.
material_facts: The plaint repeatedly asserted that the plaintiffs were co-owners in joint possession and sought partition and separate possession of their shares.
The defendants disputed the plaintiffs’ possession, and the trial court made a finding about the plaintiffs’ enjoyment of the properties.
issues.conclusion: The court-fee question had to be decided by construing all material allegations in the plaint as a whole; the defendants’ pleas and the decision on the merits could not determine it.
issues.legal_principle: Following S. Rm. Ar. S. Sp. Sathappa Chettiar v. S. Ram Ar. Rm. Ramanathan Chettiar, the court held that court fee is assessed in light of the plaint’s allegations, construed as a whole, and is not affected by pleas in the written statement or the final decision on the merits.

predicates.court_fee_question_in_partition_suit: The court is determining the court fee payable in a suit seeking partition.
predicates.plaint_alleges_joint_possession: The plaintiff alleges in the plaint that they are in joint possession of the property.

issues.definition: When a court determines court fee in a partition suit and the plaint alleges joint possession, the assessment uses the plaint as a whole.

issues.legal_issue: A co-owner seeking partition is treated as being in joint possession unless excluded from possession, and court fee is payable on that basis unless the plaint clearly and specifically alleges exclusion.
material_facts: The plaintiffs claimed shares in undivided family property as heirs and alleged that they were in joint possession.

The plaint said that the defendants had not paid the plaintiffs their share of the income and that the plaintiffs could not remain in joint possession, but it also expressly claimed joint possession and sought to convert it into separate possession.
The defendants asserted that the plaintiffs were out of possession; the plaintiffs were not receiving income and were not in actual physical possession.
The plaintiffs’ entitlement to shares in the property was not disputed.
issues.conclusion: The allegations did not clearly and specifically state that the plaintiffs had been excluded from joint possession. The court fee was therefore payable under the provision for a plaintiff in joint possession, not the provision for a plaintiff excluded from possession.
issues.legal_principle: Under Section 37(1) of the Tamil Nadu Court Fees and Suits Valuation Act, court fee on market value applies when a plaintiff has been excluded from possession; Section 37(2) applies when the plaintiff is in joint possession. The general co-ownership principle is that one co-owner’s possession is in law the possession of all unless ouster or exclusion is proved. Actual physical possession or receipt of income is not necessary to remain in joint possession, so long as the right to a share and the joint nature of the property are not disputed. A clear and specific averment of exclusion in the plaint is required to apply Section 37(1). The plaintiffs’ interest by devolution was recognized under the proviso to Section 6 of the Hindu Succession Act, 1956.

rule.if: partition_suit and plaintiff_has_coownership_share and property_is_undivided_joint_property and plaint_lacks_clear_exclusion_averment and only_nonreceipt_of_income_or_lack_of_actual_possession_is_shown

predicates.partition_suit: The plaintiff brings a suit seeking partition of property and separate possession of a share.
predicates.plaintiff_has_coownership_share: The plaintiff has a legally recognized share in the property as a co-owner.
predicates.property_is_undivided_joint_property: The property remains undivided and jointly owned by the plaintiff and others.
predicates.plaint_lacks_clear_exclusion_averment: The plaint does not clearly and specifically allege that the plaintiff was excluded from joint possession.
predicates.only_nonreceipt_of_income_or_lack_of_act: The facts relied on are that the plaintiff did not receive income or was not in actual physical possession, without a clear allegation of exclusion.

issues.definition: When a co-owner seeks partition of undivided property, the plaint does not clearly allege exclusion, and only nonreceipt of income or lack of actual possession is shown, the joint-possession court-fee category applies.
